question.problem: When $p(x)=9{x}^{3}+m{x}^{2}+x-2$ is divided by $3x-1$ the remainder is $2.$ What is the value of $m?$

current_example.problem: If $q(x)=2x^3+3x^2-5x+c$ has remainder $-5$ when divided by $(x+3),$ what is the value of $c?$
current_example.worked_solution:
The remainder theorem states that when $q(x)$ is divided by $(x+3),$ the remainder equals $q(-3).$ Since we're told that the remainder is $-5,$ then, we must have $q(-3)=-5.$

Evaluating $q(-3)$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}q(-3) & =2(-3)^{3}+3(-3)^{2}-5(-3)+c \\  & =-54+27+15+c \\  & =-12+c,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that

$$
-5 = -12 + c.
$$

Solving for $c$ in the equation above, we find that $c=7.$
